title: Symbol of Hope
text: “Heroes-sama!”
Fiancée came running toward us—toward Father—the moment she arrived at the castle. Oh, and Filo-tan was there too, I say.
“I heard you’ve taken back the castle! Is Father safe?”
“Melty-chan. The Queen and the King are both safe. Well… we’ve gotten rid of the group that was occupying the castle.”
“Boo, Filo wanted to go tooo, but Spear Guy was there, so… boo.”
“Ahaha, thanks for protecting Melty-chan, Filo.”
Ahh, Filo-tan indeed. I wanted to leap at her, but Fiancée and Father were both eyeing me warily, so I couldn’t make my move.
“Vof… we come inside castle, okay?”
Wolf asked Father while glancing warily around. He must not have been able to join this time, being the Claw Hero and all.
“Well, things have settled down for the most part, so we’re inviting you in as the Queen’s guests. It also helps that there aren’t any nobles left to kick up a fuss.”
Well, it’s not like the biggest fuss-maker of all is gone. Father muttered that under his breath, brow furrowed rather conspicuously.
“Heroes-sama, Her Majesty the Queen requests your presence.”
“Well then, let’s go.”

And so… we were summoned once more to the throne room, I say. When we arrived, the Queen was standing there; she bowed once before seating herself upon the throne. Trash was made to stand beside her, though he seemed to be half-restrained by Shadow and the others surrounding him. Well, he didn’t look like he was putting up much resistance—he still seemed rather dazed from the shock of the Fairy Morph incident. Incidentally, in a different loop, the same spell hadn’t worked on Trash at all. Seems it only takes hold if the staff’s blessing has grown strong enough. The reason Trash’s “Hero” aspect—the part of him susceptible to various spells—has grown so pronounced is likely because Tiger Girl and Tiger Guy are both present this time.
“Heroes-sama, this time you have saved our beloved Melromarc from the heretical cult that unjustly seized the castle.”
“Heretical, is it? How convenient a label. Whenever it becomes inconvenient, even the state religion gets branded a heresy. Truly, might makes right, as they say.”
Itsuki gave his usual mocking little chuckle.
“…I have no words to offer in rebuttal. There will surely be those within the kingdom, and nobles who took no part in this incident, who will not accept my judgment on this…”
“Indeed! Those who drowned themselves in such extreme power are not the true Three Heroes Church! My wife! Reconsider this!”
“You wish to claim it was only a fraction of them, I suppose, but do you even understand, Aultcray, what faith the people of this kingdom currently hold?”
“That is…”
Trash’s face twisted with hesitation as his gaze drifted toward us—mainly toward Ren. Ren, feeling everyone’s eyes suddenly converge on him, glanced around in confusion. What now, of all times?

“It seems you understand well enough. Indeed. The people believe that if they worship the Sword Hero-sama, who took the lead in resolving the kingdom’s troubles, he will surely save them from the crises unfolding both within our borders and across the world…”
The Queen rose smoothly and began walking toward Ren.
“Gh… hey. That’s far enough… ugh.”
“Ren, no matter the circumstances, that attitude isn’t appropriate here.”

Ren tried to retreat as she closed the distance, but finding nowhere left to run, he gave up and steeled his expression, allowing the Queen to approach. She bowed her head to him, then took his hand. The instant she gripped it, Ren tried to pull away with his whole body, but instead found himself dragged along—ending up seated on the throne together with Fiancée, who was promptly set upon his lap as well.
“Eh? Eh? Wha—!?”
Trash, looking thoroughly reluctant, kept his silence and watched how things unfolded.
“Amaki-sama, Sword Hero, would you please, as the kingdom’s representative, take the throne in order to settle the unrest within our borders?”
“Huh? N-no, not me—surely you can’t be serious!?”
Ren, wearing an expression of pure shock, exchanged glances with Fiancée.
“You have the strong support of the citizens. Everyone believes that you, Amaki-sama, are the one most fitting to be king of our nation. Please, do be good to Melty.”

This atmosphere felt eerily similar to what had happened with Father back in the loop where he’d stayed in Melromarc and racked up far too much renown. Well, I suppose it’s because Rafumi ended up being far too active in Ren’s place this time. The symbol of hope for Melromarc—the Sword Hero, indeed! Ren was looking back and forth at us with an expression that screamed how did this happen.
“Ehh… m-mother…”
“Melty, surely you understand too?”
“T-that’s true, but…”

Hahahahaha! It seemed Fiancée’s engagement had been decided—to Ren, of all people! Fancy that—no time to bat her eyes at Father, and she ends up bound to Ren instead. How positively hilarious. This, in other words, meant that the same sort of situation that had befallen Father in that overly-virtuous loop had now befallen Ren instead. Not Father, not even Filo-tan—Ren! This was surely a chance, I say! The Queen had bestowed the throne upon Ren. By installing a hero whose accomplishments were impressive enough to satisfy the citizens, she meant to bring the current crisis under control. Trash’s authority hadn’t been stripped so much as it had simply been explained away—an impostor had seized the castle, and he’d had no choice but to flee. Hmm… Ren, king? Could he even manage it? Well, I suppose simply sitting there would probably suffice for the most part. The Queen would surely keep handling the affairs of state and official duties, and since Fiancée’s original role was essentially that anyway, even a figurehead king like Trash could get by well enough. Father, whether staying in Melromarc or serving as representative in Siltvelt, had always handled his duties properly, mind you. In any case, this seemed a sound enough plan.
“I too shall continue to act as the kingdom’s representative, but I beg of you… for the sake of our nation, please continue to save its people, now more than ever, and help calm the Waves.”
“O-oi…”
Trash, who’d shown no end of resistance when Father had been made king, seemed to have no particular objection to Ren sitting on the throne—he simply watched in silence.
“And now, allow me to offer my deepest apologies for dragging you, Heroes-sama, into this incident.”
So saying, the Queen bowed her head deeply.
“No problem at all. Honestly, it’s a relief thinking my false charges will finally be cleared. And Éclair-san can finally reclaim her territory too.”
“Indeed.”
“I might even finally be able to properly focus on that promise I made with Raphtalia-chan and the others.”
“Are you not already living here practically permanently as things stand?”
“Hey! Don’t just decide I’m king without asking me!”
While Father and the others carried on as if everything had been settled, Ren kept trying to rise from the throne, raising his voice in protest again and again.

“In any case, it has come to light that the number of nobles confirmed to remain within the kingdom has dwindled considerably. Now, with the ranks of those opposing me—those who blindly believed in the Three Heroes Church’s doctrine—thinned out as well, this is surely the time to completely purge the rot from within our nation.”
A favorable wind at the Queen’s back as well, it seemed.

“By the way, Heroes-sama, I understand that the Pope of the Three Heroes Church and certain nobles held a wicked banquet, and that the Bow Hero-sama meted out judgment for it. However, there is another matter—one severe enough to make maintaining order within the kingdom difficult—in which nobles, soldiers, and common folk alike have gone missing without a trace. I don’t suppose it would be possible for you to look into this matter as well? We have reports that some have begun returning, but the issue remains largely unresolved.”
The Queen let the question slip out to us, almost offhandedly.
“I gathered that the Bow Hero-sama’s transformation and his subsequent punishment of the kingdom’s nobles was connected to this somehow… but this trouble seems to have begun even before that.”
Her gaze shifted swiftly toward Father and Itsuki. This was clearly a matter requiring a judgment call.
“W-well, who knows? We did fight off and defeat the Three Heroes Church lot when they attacked us, but as for anything beyond that… nope, no idea.”
Once Father answered that way, everyone else seemed to fall in line with it.

Éclair looked as though she wanted to say something, but seeing Crocodile Guy let out a sigh, she kept her mouth shut after all. It seemed the Queen, too, had already more or less guessed the truth of it.
